title: Realization of supplied semilinear calculus by normalized diagram operations
statement: Fix the prime and coefficient extension of [def-pur-system-tensor-mate-arrows]. For each scheme W let a W be a supplied SemilinearDerivedSectionsData for its actual quotient sequence [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. There exist normalized diagram tensor operations o and a SemilinearPresentationComparison a o [def-pur-system-tensor-presentation-core]: its system tensor calculus is exactly a W.systems; its comparison with a.geometric retains the unit-normalized inverse-image coefficient identification, ordinary pure tensors, K-flat total model, derived units, counits, mu and geometric projection; its comparison with a.localization retains the canonical pro-etale slice sections, morphisms, horizontal transitions and ordinary open unit. No comparison with a second arbitrary normalized operations package is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0B56 equation-projection-formula-map; the agent presentation comparison Steps 1--9 in lem-pur-system-tensor-presentation-identification. These tags specify the mate word, not the concrete presentation theorem.

proof.text: Retain a W.systems on every scheme. Form the ordinary sectionwise diagram operations and their normalized tensor comparison as in the existence of TensorOperations. The constant-section unit comparison identifies each geometric inverse-image coefficient ring with the original constant quotient ring and commutes with every transition. Assemble these into the sequence ring isomorphism. Restriction along its inverse is the exact coefficient transport. Identify its pure-tensor ordinary comparison and signed total complex comparison, and descend on K-flat models.

Compare the specified ordinary geometric adjunctions with the diagram adjunction through their common sectionwise direct image and canonical coefficient map. Descend to the unbounded category using the specified derived units and system K-injectives. The tensor-model equations identify geometric mu, and substitution in its counit transpose identifies its projection. Use the slice equivalence for an open to retain every section, morphism and transition. Left-adjoint uniqueness with the actual localized restriction identifies the extension and its unit with a.localization. These data give SemilinearPresentationComparison, with systems exactly a W.systems.
